CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Placental tissue
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Fetal chromosomal analysis

TEST PERFORMED
1. Oligonucleotide Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
2. Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)

METHODOLOGY
Array CGH Analysis:
Oligonucleotide array analysis was performed on uncultured placental DNA using the GeneTech design H-5030 platform. This array contains approximately 60,000 oligonucleotide probes distributed across the genome with a median effective resolution of 120kb. DNA was extracted from placental tissue, labeled, and hybridized according to manufacturer's protocols. Data analysis was performed using GenomeAnalyzer software with comparison to the GRCh37/hg19 human reference genome.

QF-PCR Analysis:
Quantitative fluorescence PCR was performed to assess for triploidy using multiple polymorphic markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y.

RESULTS

Array CGH Result:
arr(1-22,X,Y)x2

No copy number imbalances of known fully penetrant pathogenicity were detected.

The array results are consistent with a normal male chromosome complement.

QF-PCR Result:
No evidence of triploidy detected. Diallelic patterns observed for all informative markers tested.

INTERPRETATION
Array CGH analysis of uncultured placental DNA showed no chromosomal imbalances of known clinical significance. The results indicate a normal male karyotype with no detectable pathogenic copy number variants at the resolution of this array.

The QF-PCR analysis excluded triploidy and confirmed normal copy number for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y.

TEST LIMITATIONS
- This array has a median effective resolution of 120kb. Smaller copy number variants below this resolution may not be detected.
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements, low-level mosaicism (<20%), and point mutations are not detectable by this method.
- Array CGH cannot detect polyploidy; however, QF-PCR was performed to exclude triploidy.
- Uniparental disomy and methylation abnormalities are not assessed by this test.
- The clinical significance of copy number variants is based on current knowledge and may change as new information becomes available.

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is required for this sample based on current findings.
